product.olivetti-m211v.summary: The VGA variant of the M211 laptop, with a 32-shade display and memory expandable through a 1 or 4 MB card.
product.olivetti-m211v.history: The M211V expanded the M211 portable family with VGA graphics for work away from the office. Olivetti’s English brochure is dated February 1990 and an advertisement in The Computer Paper offers it in April that year. Marketing targeted professionals needing DOS, OS/2 or XENIX and connections to desktop peripherals. A photographed board bears “PEGASUS INC.” and “MADE IN JAPAN”; the ISER collection attributes manufacture to Pegasus and links it to Y-E Data, although no OEM contract has been recovered here. Sources: M211V brochure, The Computer Paper and PNVA/PVGA dump photographs.
product.olivetti-m211v.warning: Historical sheet under research. BluMach retains an incomplete experimental implementation; this sheet does not enable its selection or profile creation.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.market: Period documentation places its availability before 1991. The English brochure says 02/90 and the German one 3.90; ISER’s XP1023V unit is catalogued as made in 1991, which does not date the launch of the entire range.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.configu: Different disk and memory options were sold. The brochures offer 20 or 40 MB disks, a 1.44 MB floppy drive and 1 MB RAM; the April 1990 advertisement combines a 40 MB disk, carrying case, Paranet and MS-DOS 4.01 as a specific offer.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.memory: Expansion used an additional card rather than requiring a new computer. The brochures describe an initial 1 MB and 1 or 4 MB cards giving 2 or 5 MB; some memory can be used as extended memory or LIM EMS 4.0.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.video: The internal display is backlit monochrome VGA. The brochures specify 640 × 480 pixels, 32 grey shades, contrast and illumination controls and an external VGA monitor connection; it should not be confused with the M211’s EGA LCD.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.expansi: Office peripherals and an expansion card could be connected. The brochure lists RS-232C, Centronics, PS/2 keyboard/mouse, an external numeric keypad and a 16-bit slot for a half-length card, limited to 6.8 W.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.firmwar: One dump contains both system and video. The 128 KiB PNVA/PVGA 1.03 divides into 48 KiB video, a zero-filled 16 KiB window and 64 KiB system; derivatives match those regions byte for byte. In the original file, 0x001E identifies Stingray and 0x1E02B the system version.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.board: Photographs allow board markings to be read without assigning them to every M211. PEGASUS INC., PNVA/PVGA 1.03, PKCA 1.03, C&T F82C241 and Toshiba TC8565AF are visible. The brochures specify 16/8 MHz; the ISER record says 12 MHz and the discrepancy remains unresolved.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.verifie: The existing code loads the system at F0000h and video ROM at E0000h. The record reports an earlier POST reaching code 65 and Setup entry with incomplete text and keyboard input; this session checks documents, files and code only, without repeating the boot.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.limitat: The implementation retains NEAT chipset and GD5401 video approximations for the laptop hardware. Power, LCD, Setup, CMOS, disk and memory validation remain pending; the code offers 1 or 5 MB, not the commercial 2 MB option. The historical sheet does not enable the model in the public release.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.brochur: Olivetti, Personal Computer M211V: English 02/90 and German 3.90 brochures, two pages each. Originals preserved and pages visually reviewed; cover prepared for the website only.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.advert_: The Computer Paper, vol. 3, no. 4, April 1990, Olivetti advertisement, PDF page 33: a 16 MHz M211V offer with a 40 MB disk. Issue preserved.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.museum_: ISER, inventory I1889, 23 January 2023: a 1991 XP1023V unit and Pegasus/Y-E Data attribution. It says 12 MHz against 16/8 MHz in the brochures; this is not turned into a confirmed revision.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.firmwar: TiBo’s Retro Computers, PNVA/PVGA 1.03 dump and board photographs, preserved from Internet Archive. Static check; original firmware and images remain outside Git.
product.olivetti-m211v.technical.code_so: BluMach 88f74ba3, m_at_olivetti_m211v.c and GD5401 video configuration. Experimental implementation added after the fork; its approximations are not real-machine specifications.
